name: data-structure-visualizer

dsv.compiler.description: C++ compiler executable (also used to build the allocation shim, even for C programs).

dsv.cCompiler.description: C compiler executable, used for .c files.

dsv.extraCFlags.description: Extra flags for .c files. -O0 -g are always forced.

dsv.subSteps.description: Show intermediate states inside a source line that holds several statements (a one-line swap). Off = one step per line.

dsv.maxSubStepsPerLine.description: Most intermediate stops per execution of one line; a line over this is read whole (like before).

dsv.maxSubStepsPerRun.description: Most intermediate stops in one run; afterwards lines are read whole.

dsv.maxMemoryMB.description: Virtual-memory cap (MB) for the traced process tree. 0 = unlimited.

dsv.sandbox.description: auto: run the traced program inside bubblewrap when it is installed and works (read-only filesystem, private /tmp, $HOME hidden, no network). Falls back to isolateNetwork-only otherwise.

dsv.isolateNetwork.description: Run the traced program in a new network namespace when the OS allows it (best effort; not a full sandbox).

dsv.args.description: Command-line arguments for the program (argv[1], argv[2], ...). Each item is one argument, passed as is (no shell quoting needed). No newline characters.

dsv.stdin.description:
Text fed to the program's standard input, e.g. "3
10 20 30
" (a JSON string: 
 is a newline). Empty means the program sees end-of-file. Up to 1 MiB.

dsv.stdinFile.description: A file whose contents are fed to the program's standard input; a relative path is relative to the folder of the file you visualize. Takes precedence over dsv.stdin.

description: Visualize your own C and C++ data-structure implementations step by step, from real execution.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: echo build via root npm run build
